questions.question: Analyze the relationship between power and landscape in Tintin's travels
questions.solution_html:
• Tintin in Congo - humans overpower nature – European colonial force against African
  • landscape – Tintin takes part in big game hunting (popular among whites) and slaughters
  • animals for their skin and tusk. Tintin in Tibet – power struggle between nature and humans –
  • nature possessing a dominant hand.

questions.question: What contrast does the essay highlight between Tintin in the Congo and Tintin in Tibet?
questions.solution_html:
• Tintin in Congo – ecological exploitation of the land of the colonized – Tintin appears as a
  • superior European figure – Africa as an exotic land – Reflects colonial ideology (Europeans
  • as civilizers). Tintin in Tibet – vast Himayalan landscape – Tintin is vulnerable and dependent
  • – Nature is a dominant, threatening force that challenges humans.
questions.final_answer: – Nature is a dominant, threatening force that challenges humans
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Comment on The Jungle Book as an intertext.
questions.solution_html:
• The Jungle Book - forms an intertextual web – draws on traditions of Aesop’s fables –
  • RKJB (Rudyard Kipling’s Jungle Book) itself is fragmented – The presence of “In the Rukh,”
  • which features an adult Mowgli, demonstrates intratextuality within Rudyard Kipling’s own
  • works. The text is also indebted to multiple pre-texts, including colonial ethnographic
  • writings like Beast and Man in India, adventure fiction such as “Nada the Lily”, and elements
  • of Hindu mythology, especially in its emphasis on law, hierarchy, and order. Thus, The Jungle
  • Book functions not merely as a single narrative but as a signifier within a larger intertextual
  • system, influencing and shaping later representations of jungle life and animal societies. In
  • this sense, it becomes a hegemonic text, capable of defining the genre it belongs to.
questions.final_answer: this sense, it becomes a hegemonic text, capable of defining the genre it belongs to
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: How did Cinderella's step-sisters treat her?
questions.solution_html:
• Cinderella – classic fairy-tale motif of a persecuted heroine. Stepsisters – cruelty, jealousy
  • and arrogance – treated Cinderella as a servant – forced her to do all household chores –
  • mocked at her dirty appearance – excluded her socially – moral ugliness.
questions.final_answer: mocked at her dirty appearance – excluded her socially – moral ugliness
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the relationship between Mufasa and Scar?
questions.solution_html:
• The relationship between Mufasa and Scar in The Lion King is complex, shaped by
  • brotherhood, rivalry, jealousy, and betrayal. It forms the central conflict of the story – Mufasa
  • and Scar are brothers, but Mufasa is the rightful king and Scar is the younger, sidelined
  • sibling – Scar envies Mufasa because he holds power and respect, and his son Simba will
  • inherit the throne. Scar feels inferior and overlooked, which turns into deep resentment –
  • Scar’s jealousy leads him to plot Mufasa’s death and betray his own brother during the
  • stampede.
questions.final_answer: stampede
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Discuss Superman as a modernist and sacred hero with reference to the values, grand narratives, and moral vision presented in “Superman: a Modernist Hero.”
questions.solution_html:
• Superman - a cultural phenomenon (American Cultural narratives) – 9/11 attack – an end
  • of postmodernism in America – Superhero movies and Metanarratives re-emerged – Grand
  • narratives of truth, justice, democracy relapsed – Modernist hero – Superman chooses
  • violence to fight against evils rather than relying on the institutional justice – a response to
  • modernist existential chaos –Superman as a Messianic figure – His existence is mythical and
  • sacred, imbued with values – His moral vision – no ambiguity in right and wrong.
questions.final_answer: sacred, imbued with values – His moral vision – no ambiguity in right and wrong
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Critically assess the psychological and physical development of Mowgli—The Man-Cub—as portrayed in the 1989 television series Janguru Bukku Shōnen Mowgli.
questions.solution_html:
• Janguru Bukku Shonen Mowgli – Bildungsroman of Mowgli character. Physical
  • development – weakness to mastery of jungle – depends on the wolf pack for survival. His
  • body becomes attuned to the jungle, almost animal-like – Torn between jungle (freedom
  • instinct) and society (reason, culture) – Emotional growth through loss, betrayal, experiences
  • – The Boomerang cements his strength and confidence – The real psychological
  • development: Mowgli accepts his position in the man-village and 'outgrows the jungle'.
questions.final_answer: development: Mowgli accepts his position in the man-village and 'outgrows the jungle'
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explore the moral complexities presented in "Sun, Pearl and Anna."
questions.solution_html:
• Princess Anna – passive heroine v/s ideal femininity – silenced subject – Marriage is not
  • a choice, but an inevitable destiny – prince hides his marriage from mother – morality is
  • situational – Jealous and ogre mother-in-law tries to eat grandchildren namely Sun and Pearl
  • – Maternal instinct is inverted to violence – Dangers in family
questions.final_answer: – Maternal instinct is inverted to violence – Dangers in family
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Analyse "The Company of Wolves" as a feminist retelling of the "Little Red Riding Rood" tale.
questions.solution_html:
• Traditional tale – Little Red Riding Hood is naïve, helpless and a victim of the wolf. In
  • Carter’s version, the girl is bold, fearless and self-aware – female innocence to female agency
  • – wolf is a symbol of patriarchy – she challenges male aggression and predatory desire –
  • tames the wolf in the end.
